intro.text: This entry describes oocyte/zygote/embryo maturation arrest-26 (OZEMA26), a form of female infertility in which oocytes, zygotes or early embryos fail to develop normally during assisted reproduction.

checks.claim: Oocyte/zygote/embryo maturation arrest-26 (OZEMA26) is a form of female infertility.
checks.evidence_quote: biallelic mutations in MEI1 were also associated with early embryonic arrest and recurrent implantation failure
checks.explanation: The abstract describes MEI1-related female infertility (early embryonic arrest) but never uses the name OZEMA26; that designation is not in the abstract.

checks.claim: In OZEMA26, oocytes, zygotes or early embryos fail to develop normally during assisted reproduction.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified several novel mutations in MEI1 causing new phenotypes of early embryonic arrest and recurrent implantation failure.
checks.explanation: The abstract supports early embryonic arrest. It does not say that oocytes or zygotes fail, or describe the assisted-reproduction setting in detail.

paragraphs.text: Oocyte/zygote/embryo maturation arrest (OZEMA) is a group of female infertility disorders found during in vitro fertilization (IVF) or intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) cycles. Affected women have normal menstrual cycles and hormone levels. However, their retrieved oocytes arrest before maturation, fail to fertilize, or form zygotes and early embryos that arrest or degenerate. As a result, the women have recurrent failure of assisted reproduction.

checks.claim: Oocyte/zygote/embryo maturation arrest (OZEMA) is a group of female infertility disorders.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 5 cited papers. The abstract does not define OZEMA as a group of disorders.

checks.claim: OZEMA is found during in vitro fertilization (IVF) or intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) cycles.
checks.evidence_quote: Embryonic developmental arrest (EDA), characterized by the cessation of embryo growth at early stages from zygote to blastocyst, poses significant challenges in vitro fertilization (IVF) cycles.
checks.explanation: The paper places EDA in the setting of IVF cycles but does not discuss OZEMA as a category.

checks.claim: Women affected by OZEMA have normal menstrual cycles.
checks.evidence_quote: She had regular menstrual cycles and a normal ovarian reserve.
checks.explanation: Both probands had regular menstrual cycles, but the paper does not generalise this to OZEMA.

checks.claim: Women affected by OZEMA have normal hormone levels.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 5 cited papers. The abstract does not mention hormone levels.

checks.claim: In OZEMA, retrieved oocytes may arrest before maturation.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 5 cited papers. The abstract does not mention oocyte maturation arrest.

checks.claim: In OZEMA, retrieved oocytes may fail to fertilize.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 5 cited papers. The abstract does not mention fertilization failure.

checks.claim: In OZEMA, retrieved oocytes may form zygotes and early embryos that arrest or degenerate.
checks.evidence_quote: Apart from recurrent hydatidiform moles, biallelic mutations in MEI1 were also associated with early embryonic arrest and recurrent implantation failure.
checks.explanation: The abstract supports early embryonic arrest in MEI1 patients only. It does not describe OZEMA in general, zygote arrest or degeneration.

checks.claim: Women with OZEMA have recurrent failure of assisted reproduction.
checks.evidence_quote: We then expanded the mutational screening to patients with the phenotype of embryonic arrest, recurrent implantation failure, and recurrent pregnancy loss
checks.explanation: The abstract supports recurrent implantation failure in MEI1 patients but does not generalize to OZEMA.

paragraphs.text: OZEMA is genetically heterogeneous. Different forms are caused by mutations in genes for zona pellucida proteins, oocyte meiotic and cytoskeletal regulators, subcortical maternal complex components, and regulators of maternal mRNA decay. This entry is one numbered form in that series.

checks.evidence_quote: Mutations in maternal effect genes have been implicated in EDA, which was discussed in recent literatures.
checks.explanation: The paper implies that several genes are involved in EDA but does not state that OZEMA is genetically heterogeneous.

checks.claim: Some forms of OZEMA are caused by mutations in genes encoding zona pellucida proteins.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 5 cited papers. The abstract does not mention zona pellucida genes.

checks.claim: Some forms of OZEMA are caused by mutations in genes encoding oocyte meiotic and cytoskeletal regulators.
checks.evidence_quote: Our results not only reveal the important role of MEI1 in human oocyte meiosis and early embryonic development
checks.explanation: The abstract implicates one meiotic gene (MEI1) in embryonic arrest. It says nothing about cytoskeletal regulators or the OZEMA classification.

checks.claim: Some forms of OZEMA are caused by mutations in genes encoding subcortical maternal complex components.
checks.evidence_quote: Maternal effect genes, such as those encoding the subcortical maternal complex (SCMC), governs these processes. Mutations in maternal effect genes have been implicated in EDA
checks.explanation: The paper links SCMC/maternal-effect genes to EDA only in general terms, without referring to numbered OZEMA forms.

checks.claim: Some forms of OZEMA are caused by mutations in genes encoding regulators of maternal mRNA decay.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 5 cited papers. The abstract does not mention maternal mRNA decay.
